ended: Lost the NBA Finals 1-4 to NY

archetype.name: Conference Champion (defense-first)
archetype.definition: A team that went from 34 wins to the league's best record and a Western Conference title on a Wembanyama-anchored defense, then lost a Finals full of close games when its half-court scoring dried up.

report.headline: From 34 wins to the Finals, undone by a cold offense and coin flips

recap.finish: 62-20, first in the Southwest; won the West, lost the NBA Finals 1-4 to NY
recap.body:
This was not a gradual climb. A year ago San Antonio went 34-48 with the league's 25th-ranked defense. This season it went 62-20, finished first on the site's Teams tab, posted a Net Rtg of 8.3 (second in the league) and ranked in the top four on both ends, with a 119.6 offensive rating and a 111.3 defensive rating. Houston's 52-30 was the only other winning record in the Southwest, and it wasn't close. The record was earned on the margin: the differential implies 60 wins, so close-game luck added only a couple.

The path had two speeds. A 5-0 October gave way to a choppy 8-6 November, an 11-3 December and an 8-7 January in which the offense fell to 110.53 points a game, easily its worst month. Then the team took over. It went 11-0 in February and 14-2 in March, and it closed 8-2 over its last ten, with both losses to Denver, one of them in overtime. It never lost more than two straight all season.

Victor Wembanyama drove it. He scored 1,600 points on a 62.6 TS %, posted a 10.7 BPM and a +16 On-Off, ranked first on the center tab, and won Defensive Player of the Year on top of All-NBA First Team. The defense he anchored won by contesting shots and finishing possessions rather than forcing mistakes. Opponents shot a 52.2 eFG % against a league average of 54.6, and the Spurs' DRB % was the best in the league, but their Opp TOV % ranked 26th. The offense was efficient without being a shooting show: TS % ranked fifth and TOV % fifth, while 3P % sat exactly at the league average. Around the star the depth graded A in both the backcourt and on the wings. De'Aaron Fox made the All-Star team, Stephon Castle handed out 502 assists, Julian Champagnie posted a +9.7 On-Off in all 82 games, and Keldon Johnson won Sixth Man of the Year on a 61.3 TS %.

The playoff run tested every layer. Portland fell 4-1 and Minnesota 4-2, the latter closed with 29- and 30-point wins. Against Oklahoma City the Spurs were down three games to two before winning 118-91 at home and 111-103 on the road in Game 7. The Finals against New York turned on inches. San Antonio dropped both home openers, 95-105 and 104-105, won Game 3 on the road, then lost 106-107 and 90-94. The defense held all spring: the postseason Opp eFG % of 48.2 was the best of the 16 playoff teams. The scoring did not. It fell from 119.83 a game in the regular season to 112.39, with Fox (49.7 TS %), Johnson (49.2) and Harrison Barnes (49.5) all going cold. The postseason W vs Pt Diff of -4 ranked last among playoff teams, so the close games that had been a non-issue all winter went the wrong way when they mattered most.

The verdict: this was a genuine elite team, not a hot streak. Its playoff Net Rtg of 7.6 ranked second, and it beat three playoff opponents before running into a Finals where two one-point losses decided the series. The flaws that showed up, secondary scoring that wilted and a defense that rarely forced turnovers, are specific and fixable. They are not signs that the 62 wins were a mirage.

highlights.title: Wembanyama built an elite defense
highlights.body: The defense went from 25th to third in a season. Opponents' shooting fell well below the league average, and the team owned the defensive glass. Wembanyama's +16 On-Off and Defensive Player of the Year award put the source in one place, and the defense got even stingier in the playoffs. As long as he is on the floor, this carries over.

highlights.title: A record backed by the margin
highlights.body: The 62 wins rested on the second-best Net Rtg in the league, not on close-game escapes. The differential implied 60 wins, and an 11-0 February and 14-2 March were blowout-driven. That makes the regular-season level a credible baseline rather than a peak to regress from.

highlights.title: Deep, efficient guards and wings
highlights.body: Both perimeter groups graded A. Fox, Castle and Dylan Harper split the ball-handling, Champagnie's +9.7 On-Off led the non-Wembanyama regulars, and Johnson won Sixth Man of the Year. In the playoffs Harper (61.1 TS %, 3.7 BPM) and Champagnie (4.6 BPM) were the secondary pieces who actually held up.

lowlights.title: Secondary scoring vanished in June
lowlights.body: Playoff scoring fell to 112.39 a game from 119.83 in the regular season, and the Finals produced 95, 90 and two one-point losses. The drop traces to the second options: Fox's TS % fell to 49.7 and Johnson's to 49.2, with a -2.9 BPM. Wembanyama kept producing, but the offense around him leaned too heavily on him when the defense tightened.

lowlights.title: Close games flipped at the end
lowlights.body: After a season with almost no close-game luck either way, the playoff W vs Pt Diff of -4 ranked dead last among the 16 teams. The Finals were the sharpest case: three of the four losses came by four points or fewer. Some of that is noise that evens out, but it also ties back to a half-court offense that couldn't find a basket late.

lowlights.title: Thin frontcourt behind the star
lowlights.body: The frontcourt graded only B-, despite the league's top-ranked center, because the minutes around him were weak. Carter Bryant posted a -3 BPM over 818 minutes and Kelly Olynyk a -17.9 On-Off. Barnes graded middling and went cold in the playoffs. This is a roster gap rather than bad luck, and it is the clearest group to upgrade.

arc.note: An uneven first three months, capped by an 8-7 January with the season's weakest offense, gave way to an 11-0 February and 14-2 March. The team carried that level through three playoff rounds before the Finals offense stalled.

recap.nextYear: The foundation is real and carries over. A margin-built 62 wins, a top-three defense and the league's best defensive rebounding all run through Wembanyama, whose 10.7 BPM and 10 Win Shares came in only 64 games. The A-graded backcourt and wings should hold, and Harper's and Champagnie's playoff numbers suggest those roles can grow. The work is in two places. The frontcourt minutes behind Wembanyama graded B- and bled points when he sat. The defense also forced turnovers at a bottom-five rate. The Finals' run of narrow losses was partly bad luck, but the playoff scoring slump among Fox, Johnson and Barnes was a real shortfall, and the team needs a second creator who holds up when the game slows down.

confidence.note: Full 82-game season plus 23 playoff games; Finals sample is five games.
